description: Renovate covers vertical-pod-autoscaler only; the rest of the repository uses Dependabot. Restrictions are expressed via matchUpdateTypes rather than `enabled: false`, because dep-level disables are applied before version lookup and cannot be re-enabled per update type.

customManagers.description: Track the golangci-lint and kube-api-linter pins of the custom kube-api-linter build without adding their dependencies to hack/tools/go.mod.
Track the golangci-lint version used by the golangci-lint GitHub Action (version-file input). The file holds nothing but the version, so depName and datasource are templated.

packageRules.description: The custom kube-api-linter build is updated as one unit: both golangci-lint pins and the kube-api-linter plugin, which must be compatible with each other.
The CI golangci-lint pin (.golangci-lint-version) is independent of the custom kube-api-linter build and gets its own PR. Must come after the kube-api-linter grouping rule to override its groupName.
golangci-lint major upgrades require changing the /v2 module path manually.
Release branches: the custom kube-api-linter build is only updated on master. kube-api-linter is untagged, so its pseudo-version tracks default-branch commits and is never patch-level.
Docker images: patch updates only, on every branch. Go minor bumps are done manually.
Docker images: one PR per branch, checked daily.
Go modules: only propose versions whose go.mod `go` directive is satisfied by ours, so dependency bumps never force a Go minor bump.
Go modules: also update indirect dependencies. Rules that restrict indirect updates must come after this one.
Go modules: indirect dependencies cannot be moved to a new major (module path) by us; the importing dependency has to do that.

Go modules: pre-modules +incompatible pseudo-versions cannot follow newer commits once upstream adds a go.mod with a /vN module path (e.g. github.com/mistifyio/go-zfs -> /v4); the importing dependency has to make that move.
Go modules: github.com/euank/go-kmsg-parser's v2.0.1 tag ships a go.mod without the /v2 module path, so Go rejects it; stay on v2.0.0+incompatible.

Go modules: github.com/mmarkdown/mmark gained a go.mod with a /v2 module path at v2.2.x, so tags beyond v2.0.40+incompatible are not valid on the old path; the importing dependency (crd-ref-docs) has to make that move.
Go modules: fsnotify is locked at 1.9.0 on every branch, matching the gomodguard restriction in vertical-pod-autoscaler/.golangci.yaml (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138865).
Kubernetes modules: patch updates only, on every branch. This also blocks the independent digest bumps of untagged k8s.io/kube-openapi and k8s.io/utils, which must track the apimachinery release.
Kubernetes modules: one PR per branch, checked daily. separateMinorPatch makes Renovate offer the highest patch even though the minor is blocked.
Everything that is not a Kubernetes module goes into one PR per branch, checked weekly (the repository default). On master this means latest versions; the release-branch rules below narrow it down.
Build tools (hack/tools/go.mod) are isolated from the product dependency graph, so their updates go into their own PR. Must come after the grouping rules above to override their groupName.
Release branches: no major, digest or replacement updates for any Go module. Digests track untagged default-branch commits, which are never patch-level.
Release branches: no minor updates either, except golang.org/x/* which are permanently pre-1.0 and ship fixes as minor bumps.
Release branches: separateMinorPatch makes Renovate offer the highest patch even though the minor is blocked.
